    Introduction

    Basic Concepts

    The pipeline

    Figure 1

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A diagram of a mock web page, showing the body as the important element, surrounded by various noise elements like navigation, cookie banners, ads, and boilerplate.’

    Figure 2

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A diagram of the curated data pipeline, showing the flow from various source formats through conversion, normalization, detection, and filtering to the shared JSONL record.’

    Figure 3

    Image 1 of 1: ‘The web data pipeline, which expands the curated pipeline earlier to include additional steps for handling raw web data, such as quality scoring, harmful-content scoring, and deduplication.’

    Figure 4

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A four-by-four similarity matrix shown as a heatmap. The diagonal is grey and labeled self. The lower triangle is blank because the matrix is symmetric. In the upper triangle, the cell for document 0 versus document 1 is fully dark at 1.00 and the cells for document 0 and document 1 versus document 2 are dark at 0.89, all three outlined in orange as duplicates above the 0.50 threshold; every cell involving the unrelated document 3 is white at 0.00.’

    Working at scale

    Figure 1

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A logarithmic deep-time scale, today at the right and the distant past at the left. Two bars show how far back nonstop reading would reach: all 173 billion raw documents about 1,2 million years, roughly four times longer than Homo sapiens has existed; the five billion survivors about 35.000 years, as old as the first cave paintings. The founding of Rome, about 2.800 years ago, sits as a thin sliver near today.’

    Figure 2

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A proportional bar of total CPU time by stage, scaled to about 31 years on one CPU core: conversion about 0,8 years (6.912 CPU hours), filtering about 5,2 years (45.810 CPU hours), and deduplication about 25,3 years (221.230 CPU hours). Deduplication dominates and runs last.’

    Figure 3

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A sorted bar chart of pipeline throughput by stage, in terabytes of raw data cleared per day. Upload completion about 25, deduplication about 20, conversion about 20, quality signals about 6,4, and download about 6,2. The two slowest stages, quality signals and download, are highlighted; at about 6 terabytes a day, about 725 terabytes take roughly 116 days.’

    The quality question

    Figure 1

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A two-by-two grid. The horizontal axis is form, from poorly formed on the left to well-formed on the right. The vertical axis is value, from low at the bottom to high at the top. A vertical dashed line down the middle marks where a surface heuristic cuts: it keeps everything on the well-formed right half and drops the left half, regardless of value. Two corners are shaded as errors: the top-left, substantive but messy documents that the heuristic wrongly drops, and the bottom-right, well-formed but worthless documents such as spam that it wrongly keeps. Examples sit in each quadrant: an encyclopedia article top-right, spam bottom-right, a nav menu bottom-left, dense code or terse notes top-left.’

    Figure 2

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A line chart on logarithmic axes (cost against number of documents) with three points on one straight line. Judging one million documents costs about 300 euros; fourteen million about 4.200 euros; and five billion, the full surviving corpus, about 1,5 million euros. Cost rises in proportion to the number of documents.’

    Cheap proxies for good text

    Figure 1

    Image 1 of 1: ‘A log-log scatter plot. The horizontal axis is the number of documents a judgment runs on, from ten thousand to a trillion; the vertical axis is cost per document in euros. Three judgment tiers fall on a downward line from top-left to bottom-right: human review of a curated seed at about 10 euro per document; the LLM judge at about 0,0003 euro per document over the roughly 5 billion survivors; and surface filters plus deduplication at about 0,00000007 euro per document across the whole web. An open marker at the bottom right is the raw web of 173 billion documents, ungraded.’
